absolut.explanation: "Absolut" means "absolutely" and makes a word stronger: Han har absolut ret (He is absolutely right).

sentence.da: Det er **absolut** umuligt at nå toget nu.
sentence.en: It is absolutely impossible to catch the train now.

abstrakt.explanation: "Abstrakt" means "abstract", about thoughts and qualities rather than things you can touch. In art, it describes pictures that do not show real objects: abstrakt kunst (abstract art).

sentence.da: Frihed er et **abstrakt** begreb.
sentence.en: Freedom is an abstract concept.

absurd.explanation: "Absurd" means "absurd", used for something so unreasonable that it makes no sense, whether it is a price, an excuse or a rule.

sentence.da: Det er **absurd**, at en kop kaffe koster tohundrede kroner.
sentence.en: It is absurd that a cup of coffee costs two hundred kroner.

adfærd.explanation: "En adfærd" means "behavior", the way a person or an animal acts over time, not one single act. For one single act, use en handling (an action).

sentence.da: Barnets **adfærd** i skolen er blevet bedre.
sentence.en: The child's behavior at school has improved.

adgang.explanation: "Adgang" means "access" or "entry", the right to get in or to use something. It is followed by til (to): Vi har ikke adgang til rummet (We do not have access to the room).

sentence.da: Med dette kort får du **adgang** til hotellet.
sentence.en: With this card you get access to the hotel.

adopteret.explanation: "Adopteret" means "adopted", taken into a family as your own child: Hun er adopteret fra Kina (She is adopted from China). It comes from at adoptere (to adopt).

sentence.da: Hun er **adopteret** og kom til Danmark som baby.
sentence.en: She is adopted and came to Denmark as a baby.

adskillige.explanation: "Adskillige" means "several", a large number, more than a handful, without giving the exact number. It always goes before words in the plural.

sentence.da: Der kom **adskillige** gæster til festen.
sentence.en: Several guests came to the party.

adskilt.explanation: "Adskilt" means "separated", kept apart and not joined. For a couple who are divorced, Danes say skilt (divorced): De er skilt (They are divorced).

sentence.da: Køkkenet og stuen er **adskilt** af en tynd væg.
sentence.en: The kitchen and the living room are separated by a thin wall.

af og til.explanation: "Af og til" means "now and then", for things that happen once in a while, not every day. Compare Jeg drikker kaffe hver dag (I drink coffee every day) with Jeg drikker kaffe af og til (I drink coffee now and then).

forms.da: jeg går i biografen af og til
forms.en: I go to the movie theater now and then

sentence.da: Vi ses ikke ofte, kun **af og til**.
sentence.en: We do not see each other often, only now and then.

afdød.explanation: "Afdød" means "deceased", a respectful word for someone who is no longer alive, used in obituaries and about family: min afdøde far (my late father).

sentence.da: Min bedstemor er **afdød**, og vi savner hende.
sentence.en: My grandmother is deceased, and we miss her.

affald.explanation: "Affald" means "trash". You do not count it: Der er meget affald på gaden (There is a lot of trash on the street). One bag of it is en pose affald (a bag of trash).

sentence.da: Vi smider **affald** i skraldespanden.
sentence.en: We throw trash in the trash can.

afgjort.explanation: "Afgjort" means "decided" or "settled", something that is no longer open. Before a word like bedre (better), it means "for sure", with no doubt.

sentence.da: Efter den sidste runde var det **afgjort**, hvem der havde vundet.
sentence.en: After the last round it was decided who had won.

afgørende.explanation: "Afgørende" means "decisive" or "crucial", something that settles the outcome, so that everything depends on it. It is stronger than vigtig (important).

sentence.da: Det sidste mål var **afgørende** for, hvem der vandt.
sentence.en: The last goal was decisive for who won.

afhængig.explanation: "Afhængig" means "dependent" or "addicted", and is used with af (of): Jeg er afhængig af kaffe (I am addicted to coffee). Det er afhængigt af vejret (It depends on the weather).

sentence.da: Min lillebror er **afhængig** af sin telefon.
sentence.en: My little brother is addicted to his phone.

afhængig af.explanation: "Afhængig af" means "dependent on", needing something or being tied to it. It also covers addiction: Han er afhængig af sin telefon (He is hooked on his phone). To say it depends on, use at afhænge af: Det afhænger af prisen (It depends on the price).

sentence.da: En baby er **afhængig af** sine forældre.
sentence.en: A baby is dependent on its parents.

aflyst.explanation: "Aflyst" means "canceled", for example a train, a flight or an event that will not take place. It is different from forsinket (delayed): a delayed train still comes, but a canceled one does not.

sentence.da: Toget er **aflyst** i dag.
sentence.en: The train is canceled today.

afmagt.explanation: "En afmagt" means "powerlessness", the heavy feeling that you cannot change what is happening. It is made from af (away) and magt (power), so the power is taken away.

sentence.da: Han følte **afmagt**, da han ikke kunne hjælpe sit barn.
sentence.en: He felt powerless when he could not help his child.

afpresning.explanation: "Afpresning" means "blackmail", forcing someone to give money or do something by frightening them, for example by saying you will reveal a secret. The verb is at afpresse (to blackmail).

sentence.da: Han blev anklaget for **afpresning**, fordi han krævede penge for at tie.
sentence.en: He was accused of blackmail because he demanded money to keep quiet.

afrika.explanation: "Afrika" means "Africa". It is spelled with a k, not a c as in English. Add syd (south) to get Sydafrika (South Africa).

sentence.da: Løver og elefanter lever i **Afrika**.
sentence.en: Lions and elephants live in Africa.

afrikansk.explanation: "Afrikansk" means "African" and describes things from Africa: afrikansk musik (African music). For a person, use en afrikaner (an African).

sentence.da: Løven er et **afrikansk** dyr.
sentence.en: The lion is an African animal.

afslappet.explanation: "Afslappet" means "relaxed", for a person or a mood: Han er meget afslappet (He is very relaxed). Stemningen var afslappet (The mood was relaxed).

sentence.da: Efter ferien er jeg meget **afslappet**.
sentence.en: After the vacation, I am very relaxed.

afsted.explanation: "Afsted" means "off" or "away", for leaving a place. Compare Jeg er hjemme (I am at home) with Jeg skal afsted (I have to go off).

sentence.da: Hej hej, jeg skal **afsted** nu.
sentence.en: Bye bye, I have to go now.

aftensmad.explanation: "Aftensmad" means "dinner". It is built from aften (evening) and mad (food). It is the everyday word for dinner at home: Hvad skal vi have til aftensmad? (What are we having for dinner?)

sentence.da: Om aftenen spiser vi **aftensmad** sammen.
sentence.en: In the evening we eat dinner together.

afvænning.explanation: "Afvænning" means "rehab" and "detox", the process of getting free of a habit such as alcohol or drugs. It is built from af (off) and at vænne (to accustom): you get out of the habit, and fra (from) names the habit.

sentence.da: Efter flere år med alkohol startede han på **afvænning**.
sentence.en: After several years with alcohol, he started rehab.

aggressiv.explanation: "Aggressiv" means "aggressive", ready to attack or shout: Han bliver aggressiv, når han er sur (He gets aggressive when he is grumpy). It is used for people, animals and words.

sentence.da: Hunden er **aggressiv** og viser tænderne.
sentence.en: The dog is aggressive and shows its teeth.

akademisk.explanation: "Akademisk" means "academic", about higher education and scholarly work. A person with a degree is en akademiker (a graduate).

sentence.da: Hun har taget en **akademisk** uddannelse på universitetet.
sentence.en: She has completed an academic education at the university.

akavet.explanation: "Akavet" means "awkward", for a situation that feels uncomfortable, such as a first date or a sudden question.

sentence.da: Det blev **akavet**, da ingen sagde noget.
sentence.en: It got awkward when nobody said anything.

aktiv.explanation: "Aktiv" means "active", busy and doing things: Han er meget aktiv i klubben (He is very active in the club). It also means switched on: en aktiv konto (an active account).

sentence.da: Min bedstefar er stadig meget **aktiv** og går lange ture.
sentence.en: My grandfather is still very active and takes long walks.

aktuel.explanation: "Aktuel" means "current" or "topical", something that matters right now. It does not mean "actual": for that, use faktisk (actually).

sentence.da: Debatten om huspriserne er meget **aktuel** lige nu.
sentence.en: The debate about house prices is very topical right now.

akut.explanation: "Akut" means "acute" or "urgent", used for something that must be dealt with immediately, most of all in health. A hospital's emergency room is called en akutmodtagelse.

sentence.da: Hvis det er **akut**, skal du ringe til 112.
sentence.en: If it is urgent, you must call 112.

al.explanation: "Al" means "all" and goes in front of an en-word you do not count: al musikken (all the music). For an et-word, use alt: alt vandet (all the water).

sentence.da: Jeg har spist **al** maden.
sentence.en: I have eaten all the food.

aldeles.explanation: "Aldeles" means "entirely" or "quite", and puts more strength on the word after it. It sounds more bookish than helt (completely), which people use in everyday talk.

sentence.da: Din idé er **aldeles** genial.
sentence.en: Your idea is quite brilliant.

aldrig.explanation: "Aldrig" means "never". Compare Jeg drikker altid kaffe (I always drink coffee) with Jeg drikker aldrig kaffe (I never drink coffee). Do not add ikke (not) next to it.

sentence.da: Hun spiser **aldrig** kød.
sentence.en: She never eats meat.

alene.explanation: "Alene" means "alone" or "on your own". Compare Jeg bor alene (I live alone; nobody else is in my home) with Jeg er ensom (I feel lonely, which is a sad feeling).

sentence.da: Ingen er hjemme. Jeg er **alene**.
sentence.en: Nobody is home. I am alone.

alkohol.explanation: "Alkohol" means "alcohol". Danish does not put en (a) in front of it: Jeg drikker ikke alkohol (I do not drink alcohol). Alkoholfri øl means "alcohol-free beer".

sentence.da: Der er **alkohol** i øl og vin.
sentence.en: There is alcohol in beer and wine.

alle.explanation: "Alle" means "everyone" or "all". Alle sammen means "all together". Do not mix it up with alt (everything): Alt er her (Everything is here).

sentence.da: **Alle** børn er hjemme i dag.
sentence.en: All the children are home today.

allerede.explanation: "Allerede" means "already". Compare Han er her ikke endnu (He is not here yet) with Han er allerede her (He is already here, earlier than expected).

sentence.da: Maden er **allerede** klar.
sentence.en: The food is ready already.

allergisk.explanation: "Allergisk" means "allergic". To say what you are allergic to, add over for (to / towards): Jeg er allergisk over for nødder (I am allergic to nuts).

sentence.da: Han er **allergisk** og kan ikke spise æg.
sentence.en: He is allergic and cannot eat eggs.

alligevel.explanation: "Alligevel" means "nevertheless" and "anyway". It shows something happens despite a problem: Det regner, men vi går alligevel (It is raining, but we are going anyway).

sentence.da: Jeg er træt, men jeg kommer **alligevel**.
sentence.en: I am tired, but I am coming anyway.

almindelig.explanation: "Almindelig" means "ordinary" or "common": normal, with nothing special about it. Det er en almindelig fejl (It is a common mistake).

sentence.da: Det var bare en **almindelig** dag på arbejde.
sentence.en: It was just an ordinary day at work.

almægtig.explanation: "Almægtig" means "almighty", having all power. It is built from al (all) and mægtig (mighty). It is mostly used about God, as in Gud den almægtige (God the Almighty).

sentence.da: Mange tror på en **almægtig** gud, der har skabt verden.
sentence.en: Many believe in an almighty god who created the world.

alt.explanation: "Alt" means "everything" or "all". Compare Alle er her (Everyone is here) with Alt er her (Everything is here). Alt for means "far too": alt for dyrt (far too expensive).

sentence.da: Jeg har glemt **alt**.
sentence.en: I have forgotten everything.

alt i alt.explanation: "Alt i alt" means "all in all" and sums up what you have said: Alt i alt var det en god dag (All in all it was a good day). It usually comes at the end, after the details.

forms.da: Alt i alt går det godt.
forms.en: All in all it is going well.

sentence.da: **Alt i alt** var rejsen rigtig god.
sentence.en: All in all the trip was really good.

alternativ.explanation: "Alternativ" means "alternative", another option instead of the usual one, and also something outside the mainstream: alternativ medicin (alternative medicine). As a thing, et alternativ is the other option you can pick.

sentence.da: Vi har brug for en **alternativ** plan, hvis det regner.
sentence.en: We need an alternative plan if it rains.

altid.explanation: "Altid" means "always", every single time, with no exceptions. Compare Jeg er aldrig træt (I am never tired) with Jeg er altid træt (I am always tired).

sentence.da: Jeg står **altid** op klokken seks.
sentence.en: I always get up at six o'clock.

alting.explanation: "Alting" means "everything": Alting er dyrt her (Everything is expensive here). It often appears with ikke: Ikke alting er dyrt (Not everything is expensive).

sentence.da: Hun ved **alting** om heste.
sentence.en: She knows everything about horses.

altså.explanation: "Altså" means "so" or "then", when you sum up what was just said: Han er syg, så han kommer altså ikke (He is sick, so he is not coming). It also adds emphasis, like the English word really. Compare Det er dyrt (It is expensive) with Det er altså dyrt! (It really is expensive!).

sentence.da: Nu skal du **altså** gå i seng!
sentence.en: Now you really have to go to bed!

aluminium.explanation: "Aluminium" means "aluminum", the light, silver-colored material used in window frames, airplanes and pots. It is a material, so it normally stands alone without en or et.

sentence.da: Sodavandsdåser er lavet af **aluminium**, fordi det er let.
sentence.en: Soda cans are made of aluminum because it is light.

alverden.explanation: "Alverden" means "the whole world", said with a little exaggeration, as if nobody were left out. With an s, alverdens goes before a word and means "all kinds of".

sentence.da: Pizzaen er kendt af **alverden**.
sentence.en: Pizza is known by the whole world.

alvor.explanation: "Alvor" means "seriousness". You often use it in the phrase i alvor (seriously): Er det dit alvor? (Are you serious?). Nu er det alvor (Now it is getting serious) is what you say when the fun is over.

sentence.da: Jeg mener det i fuldt **alvor**.
sentence.en: I mean it in all seriousness.

alvorlig.explanation: "Alvorlig" means "serious", for problems and for people: Det er en alvorlig sag (It is a serious matter). Han ser alvorlig ud (He looks serious).

sentence.da: Lægen siger, at det er en **alvorlig** sygdom.
sentence.en: The doctor says that it is a serious illness.

ambitiøs.explanation: "Ambitiøs" means "ambitious" and describes a person or a goal that aims high: Hun er ambitiøs på jobbet (She is ambitious at work).

sentence.da: Hun er **ambitiøs** og vil være chef en dag.
sentence.en: She is ambitious and wants to be a boss one day.

amerikansk.explanation: "Amerikansk" means "American", used for things from the USA. It is written with a small letter, while the English word American has a capital letter.

sentence.da: Burgere er **amerikansk** mad.
sentence.en: Burgers are American food.

ammunition.explanation: "Ammunition" means "ammunition", everything that a gun or cannon fires. It is also used figuratively for facts that help you win an argument: Det giver hende ammunition (That gives her ammunition).

sentence.da: Jægeren køber **ammunition**, fordi han skal ud at skyde.
sentence.en: The hunter buys ammunition because he is going out to shoot.

anden.explanation: "Anden" means "second" and also "other". Compare min første dag (my first day) with min anden dag (my second day). Den anden bil can mean "the second car" or "the other car", and the situation tells you which. In dates: den anden juni (the second of June).

sentence.da: I dag er min **anden** dag her.
sentence.en: Today is my second day here.

anderledes.explanation: "Anderledes" means "different", as in not the usual way: Det er en anderledes film (It is a different kind of film). For things that are not alike, forskellig is common: De er forskellige (They are different).

sentence.da: Min nye skole er helt **anderledes**, ikke som den gamle.
sentence.en: My new school is completely different, not like the old one.

anger.explanation: "Anger" means "remorse", deep sorrow about something wrong you have done. It looks like the English word anger, but it is not the same: the Danish word for anger is vrede.

sentence.da: Han følte **anger** over, at han havde løjet for sin ven.
sentence.en: He felt remorse that he had lied to his friend.

angst.explanation: "Angst" means "anxiety", a strong, lasting fear that can take over everyday life, often used for the medical condition. For an ordinary fear of one thing, say frygt (fear).

sentence.da: Han har **angst** for at tale foran folk.
sentence.en: He has anxiety about speaking in front of people.

angående.explanation: "Angående" means "concerning", placed before the topic. It is common in email subject lines, such as Angående ferien (Concerning the vacation), while in speech Danes often say om (about).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver til dig **angående** din regning.
sentence.en: I am writing to you concerning your bill.

anonym.explanation: "Anonym" means "anonymous", without a name that anyone knows or shows. It is also used for places or things with no personality: en anonym lejlighed (a faceless apartment).

sentence.da: Pengene kom fra en **anonym** giver, som ingen kender.
sentence.en: The money came from an anonymous donor whom nobody knows.

anonymt.explanation: "Anonymt" means "anonymously", doing something without giving your name. It is also the et-word form of anonym (anonymous): et anonymt brev (an anonymous letter).

forms.en: She wrote anonymously to the newspaper

sentence.da: Hun gav pengene til skolen **anonymt**, uden at nævne sit navn.
sentence.en: She gave the money to the school anonymously, without mentioning her name.

anspændt.explanation: "Anspændt" means "tense", used for a situation, a person who is strained, or tight muscles. Do not mix it up with spændt (excited).

sentence.da: Stemningen var **anspændt**, og ingen turde sige noget.
sentence.en: The atmosphere was tense, and nobody dared to say anything.

anstrengende.explanation: "Anstrengende" means "strenuous" or "tiring", for something that takes a lot of effort and leaves you worn out, in body or in mind. It describes the thing, not you: for how you feel, say træt (tired).

sentence.da: Det er **anstrengende** at gå op ad bakken med tung oppakning.
sentence.en: It is tiring to walk up the hill with heavy luggage.

anstændig.explanation: "Anstændig" means "decent" in two ways: honest and respectful when said about a person, and good enough or fairly good when said about a thing, such as a meal or a result.

sentence.da: Han er en **anstændig** mand og siger altid sandheden.
sentence.en: He is a decent man and always tells the truth.

ansvarlig.explanation: "Ansvarlig" means "responsible" and describes someone you can rely on: Han er ansvarlig og kommer til tiden (He is responsible and comes on time). It also means in charge: Hvem er ansvarlig? (Who is in charge?)

sentence.da: Hun er **ansvarlig** og passer godt på sin lillebror.
sentence.en: She is responsible and takes good care of her little brother.

ansvarsfuld.explanation: "Ansvarsfuld" means "responsible" in the sense of acting with care and thinking about the results of what you do. To say who is in charge or to blame, Danes usually use ansvarlig: Han er ansvarlig for ulykken (He is responsible for the accident).

sentence.da: En **ansvarsfuld** chauffør kører langsomt, når vejen er glat.
sentence.en: A responsible driver drives slowly when the road is slippery.

antarktis.explanation: "Antarktis" means "Antarctica", the icy land at the bottom of the world. Do not mix it up with Arktis (the Arctic) in the north. Like most place names, it stands alone without en or et.

sentence.da: Næsten hele **Antarktis** er dækket af is.
sentence.en: Almost all of Antarctica is covered in ice.

antibiotika.explanation: "Antibiotika" means "antibiotics" and is used without en or et, like in English: Hun får antibiotika (She is getting antibiotics).

sentence.da: Lægen giver mig **antibiotika** mod infektionen.
sentence.en: The doctor gives me antibiotics for the infection.

anvendelig.explanation: "Anvendelig" means "usable" or "applicable", something that can be put to good use in practice, such as advice or a method. It comes from at anvende (to use).

sentence.da: Den nye metode er meget **anvendelig** i det daglige arbejde.
sentence.en: The new method is very usable in everyday work.

appelsinjuice.explanation: "Appelsinjuice" means "orange juice", a drink pressed from oranges. It is built from appelsin (orange) and juice (juice).

sentence.da: **Appelsinjuice** er en sød drik lavet af appelsiner.
sentence.en: Orange juice is a sweet drink made from oranges.

appetit.explanation: "Appetit" means "appetite", the wish for food: Jeg har ikke så meget appetit i dag (I don't have much appetite today).

sentence.da: Efter turen havde vi stor **appetit**.
sentence.en: After the trip we had a big appetite.

april.explanation: "April" means "April". Danish writes month names with a small letter, where English has a capital: i april (in April). Aprilsnar means "April fool", built from april and nar (fool).

sentence.da: Efter marts kommer **april**.
sentence.en: After March comes April.

arabisk.explanation: "Arabisk" means "Arabic", and it is used for the language and for things from the Arab world. It is written with a small letter, while the English word Arabic has a capital letter: Hun taler arabisk (She speaks Arabic).

sentence.da: Hun kommer fra Egypten og taler **arabisk**.
sentence.en: She comes from Egypt and speaks Arabic.

arbejdskraft.explanation: "Arbejdskraft" means "labor" or "workforce", the work that people can do, seen as a resource that a company or a country needs. In the plural, arbejdskræfter means the workers themselves.

sentence.da: Landet mangler **arbejdskraft**, fordi mange er gået på pension.
sentence.en: The country lacks labor because many have retired.

arbejdsløs.explanation: "Arbejdsløs" means "unemployed", without a job. It is built from arbejde (work) and løs (without), and løs works the same way in hjemløs (homeless).

sentence.da: Han har været **arbejdsløs** i tre måneder.
sentence.en: He has been unemployed for three months.

arbejdsløshed.explanation: "Arbejdsløshed" means "unemployment", the situation where many people in a country have no job. It is built from arbejdsløs, which describes one person: Han er arbejdsløs (He is unemployed).

sentence.da: Når fabrikken lukker, bliver der mere **arbejdsløshed** i byen.
sentence.en: When the factory closes, there is more unemployment in the town.

arbejdstid.explanation: "En arbejdstid" means "working hours", the hours when you are supposed to work, and also the total number of hours you work. Uden for arbejdstid means "outside working hours".

sentence.da: Min **arbejdstid** begynder klokken otte og slutter klokken seksten.
sentence.en: My working hours start at eight and end at four in the afternoon.

arkitektur.explanation: "En arkitektur" means "architecture", the art of designing buildings and also the look of the buildings in a place. It is also used for how a computer system is organized: it-arkitektur (IT architecture).

sentence.da: Husene, kirkerne og broerne i en by udgør dens **arkitektur**.
sentence.en: The houses, churches and bridges in a city make up its architecture.

arrogant.explanation: "Arrogant" means "arrogant", for a person who looks down on others and shows it in how they talk or act. It is not the same as feeling good about what you did; for that, say stolt (proud).

sentence.da: Han ser ned på alle og er meget **arrogant**.
sentence.en: He looks down on everyone and is very arrogant.

asiatisk.explanation: "Asiatisk" means "Asian" and describes things from Asia: asiatisk mad (Asian food). A person from Asia is en asiat (an Asian person).

sentence.da: Kina er et **asiatisk** land.
sentence.en: China is an Asian country.

asien.explanation: "Asien" means "Asia". The Danish spelling ends in -ien, not -ia.

sentence.da: Kina og Japan ligger i **Asien**.
sentence.en: China and Japan are in Asia.

aske.explanation: "Aske" means "ash", the gray powder that is left after something has burned. It is also the first part of et askebæger (an ashtray).

sentence.da: Efter branden var der kun **aske** tilbage i pejsen.
sentence.en: After the fire there was only ash left in the fireplace.

assistance.explanation: "Assistance" means "assistance", help from someone. It sounds more formal than hjælp (help): a clerk may ask Kan jeg være til assistance? (Can I be of assistance?), but friends say Skal jeg hjælpe dig? (Shall I help you?).

sentence.da: Kan jeg få **assistance** ved kassen?
sentence.en: Can I get assistance at the checkout?

astma.explanation: "En astma" means "asthma", a lasting lung condition where the airways narrow. You say at have astma (to have asthma).

sentence.da: Når man har **astma**, bliver det svært at trække vejret.
sentence.en: When you have asthma, it becomes hard to breathe.

at acceptere.explanation: "At acceptere" means "to accept": Jeg accepterer dit tilbud (I accept your offer). It also fits things you must live with: Hun kan ikke acceptere, at han er sen (She cannot accept that he is late).

sentence.da: Du kan **acceptere** eller sige nej til jobbet.
sentence.en: You can accept or say no to the job.

at adlyde.explanation: "At adlyde" means "to obey", to do what someone in charge tells you, such as a parent, a law or an order. It takes the person or rule directly, with no little word in between: at adlyde loven (to obey the law).

sentence.da: Børn skal **adlyde** deres forældre, når de er små.
sentence.en: Children must obey their parents when they are small.

at adskille.explanation: "At adskille" means "to separate", to keep or pull things apart, such as two groups or two parts. For a couple, Danes use the shorter at skille: De blev skilt (They got divorced).

sentence.da: Vi må **adskille** hundene, fordi de bliver ved med at slås.
sentence.en: We must separate the dogs because they keep fighting.

at advare.explanation: "At advare" means "to warn", telling someone about a danger: Jeg advarer dig mod hunden (I am warning you about the dog). The danger comes after mod (against).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **advare** dig mod den glatte vej.
sentence.en: I want to warn you about the slippery road.

at afbestille.explanation: "At afbestille" means "to cancel" something you ordered or booked: Jeg afbestiller hotelværelset (I cancel the hotel room). For an event that will not happen, use at aflyse (to call off).

forms.en: I have canceled (an order or booking)

sentence.da: Vi må **afbestille** bordet, fordi Anna er syg.
sentence.en: We have to cancel the table because Anna is sick.

at afbryde.explanation: "At afbryde" means "to interrupt" and also "to cut off", for example a connection or the power. A polite way to speak up is Undskyld, jeg afbryder (Sorry to interrupt).

sentence.da: Det er uhøfligt at **afbryde** folk, når de taler.
sentence.en: It is rude to interrupt people when they are speaking.

at afbøde.explanation: "At afbøde" means "to mitigate", to make something bad less serious, such as damage, effects or losses: at afbøde skaderne (to soften the damage). To stop it before it happens, use at afværge (to avert).

sentence.da: Kommunen vil **afbøde** virkningerne af oversvømmelsen med nye diger.
sentence.en: The municipality will mitigate the effects of the flood with new dikes.

at affyre.explanation: "At affyre" means "to fire (a weapon)", to let a gun, rocket or missile go off: at affyre en raket (to launch a rocket). To fire someone from a job, Danes say at fyre.

sentence.da: Soldaten må kun **affyre** våbnet, når han får ordre.
sentence.en: The soldier may only fire the weapon when he gets an order.

at afgive.explanation: "At afgive" means "to give off" and "to submit": a thing gives off heat or a smell (afgive varme), and a person gives a formal statement or a promise (afgive et løfte, to make a promise).

sentence.da: Når du er atten, kan du **afgive** din stemme ved valget.
sentence.en: When you are eighteen, you can cast your vote in the election.

at afgå.explanation: "At afgå" means "to depart", for trains, buses and ferries that leave at a set time. It is also used when someone gives up a position: afgå som formand (step down as chair).

sentence.da: Toget skal **afgå** klokken ti fra spor tre.
sentence.en: The train is to depart at ten from platform three.

at afgøre.explanation: "At afgøre" means "to decide" or "to settle", to bring an open question to an end: a result, a match or a case. For a personal choice, use at beslutte: Jeg har besluttet at flytte (I have decided to move).

sentence.da: Dommeren skal **afgøre**, hvem der har ret i sagen.
sentence.en: The judge must decide who is right in the case.

at afhente.explanation: "At afhente" means "to collect" or "to pick up", to take something that is waiting for you, such as an order or a package. For picking up a person, Danes more often say at hente: Jeg henter dig (I am picking you up).

sentence.da: Du kan **afhente** pakken på posthuset efter klokken to.
sentence.en: You can collect the package at the post office after two o'clock.

at afholde.explanation: "At afholde" means "to hold" a planned event, such as a meeting or an election. For holding something in your hand, say at holde. With sig fra it means "to refrain from": at afholde sig fra sukker (to stay away from sugar).

sentence.da: Skolen vil **afholde** et forældremøde i næste uge.
sentence.en: The school will hold a parents' meeting next week.

at afhænge af.explanation: "At afhænge af" means "to depend on": Det afhænger af vejret (It depends on the weather). In everyday speech, Danes often say det kommer an på instead: Det kommer an på vejret (It depends on the weather).

sentence.da: Prisen vil **afhænge af** størrelsen.
sentence.en: The price will depend on the size.

at afhøre.explanation: "At afhøre" means "to interrogate", to question someone officially, usually by the police. For an ordinary question, use at spørge (to ask).

sentence.da: Politiet vil **afhøre** manden, fordi han så ulykken.
sentence.en: The police will interrogate the man because he saw the accident.

at afkræfte.explanation: "At afkræfte" means "to disprove", to show that a claim, theory or rumor is not true. The opposite is at bekræfte (to confirm).

sentence.da: Nye tests kan **afkræfte** den gamle teori.
sentence.en: New tests can disprove the old theory.

at afkøle.explanation: "At afkøle" means "to cool down", making something less warm or letting it get cooler, such as food or an engine. You often see it in recipes: Lad kagen afkøle (Let the cake cool).

sentence.da: Is kan hurtigt **afkøle** en varm drik.
sentence.en: Ice can quickly cool a hot drink.

at aflaste.explanation: "At aflaste" means "to relieve", to take part of the weight or work off someone or something. It is built from af (off) and en last (a load), so you take some of the load away, not all of it.

sentence.da: Min bror vil **aflaste** mig ved at passe børnene i weekenden.
sentence.en: My brother will relieve me by looking after the children on the weekend.

at aflevere.explanation: "At aflevere" means "to hand in" and "to deliver": Jeg afleverer opgaven i morgen (I hand in the assignment tomorrow). It also means "to drop off": Jeg afleverer børnene i skole (I drop the kids off at school).

sentence.da: Du skal **aflevere** rapporten før fredag.
sentence.en: You have to hand in the report before Friday.

at aflyse.explanation: "At aflyse" means "to cancel", for an event, a flight or a meeting that will not happen. For your own booking, use at afbestille (to cancel an order).

sentence.da: De må **aflyse** mødet på grund af sne.
sentence.en: They have to cancel the meeting because of snow.

at aflægge.explanation: "At aflægge" means "to pay (a visit)" and "to take (an oath)". It only goes with a small set of words, such as besøg (visit), ed (oath) and regnskab (accounts): at aflægge besøg (to pay a visit). For laying something down, use at lægge.

forms.en: I have paid (a visit) / taken (an oath)

sentence.da: Vidnet skal **aflægge** ed, før hun må forklare sig i retten.
sentence.en: The witness must take an oath before she may give her statement in court.

at afmelde.explanation: "At afmelde" means "to cancel" or "to unsubscribe", taking yourself or someone else off something you signed up for, such as a course, a gym membership or a mailing list.

sentence.da: Du kan **afmelde** nyhedsbrevet nederst i mailen.
sentence.en: You can unsubscribe from the newsletter at the bottom of the email.

at afmontere.explanation: "At afmontere" means "to dismantle", to take a machine or piece of equipment off or apart, so it can be moved or repaired. It is built from af (off) and at montere (to install), so it is the opposite: you take off what was installed.

sentence.da: Vi skal **afmontere** lampen, før vi kan male loftet.
sentence.en: We must remove the lamp before we can paint the ceiling.

at afprøve.explanation: "At afprøve" means "to test" or "to try out", using something to find out how well it works, such as new equipment or a recipe.

sentence.da: Vi vil **afprøve** den nye metode på en lille gruppe.
sentence.en: We want to try out the new method on a small group.

at afsende.explanation: "At afsende" means "to send", for formally sending off goods or messages in business or official settings; in everyday talk Danes say at sende. The word afsender is also a noun: en afsender (a sender) is the person who sends the letter.

sentence.da: Butikken skal **afsende** alle ordrer, før posthuset lukker.
sentence.en: The shop must send out all orders before the post office closes.

at afskaffe.explanation: "At afskaffe" means "to abolish", to end a rule or a system for good, usually by a decision from the government or an organization. The opposite is at indføre (to introduce).

sentence.da: Regeringen vil **afskaffe** skatten på gamle biler.
sentence.en: The government wants to abolish the tax on old cars.

at afslutte.explanation: "At afslutte" means "to finish" or "to end" something on purpose. When something ends by itself, use at slutte: Filmen slutter nu (The movie ends now).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **afslutte** rapporten i dag.
sentence.en: I have to finish the report today.

at afslå.explanation: "At afslå" means "to decline" and "to refuse", to say no to a request, an offer or an application, usually officially: Kommunen afslog ansøgningen (The municipality turned down the application). For a friendly no to an invitation, Danes say at takke nej (to say no thanks).

sentence.da: Banken vil **afslå** lånet, fordi hun ikke har noget arbejde.
sentence.en: The bank will decline the loan because she has no job.

at afsløre.explanation: "At afsløre" means "to reveal", to make known something that was secret. It often means to expose a lie, a plan or a crime that someone wanted to keep out of sight.

sentence.da: Avisen vil **afsløre**, hvem der står bag svindlen.
sentence.en: The newspaper wants to expose who is behind the fraud.

at afspejle.explanation: "At afspejle" means "to reflect" in two ways: a shiny surface or water that sends back an image, and something that shows what is true: Valget afspejler, hvad folk mener (The election reflects what people think). It is not used for thinking something over; for that, say at tænke over.

sentence.da: Vandet kan **afspejle** træerne, når det er helt stille.
sentence.en: The water can reflect the trees when it is completely still.

at afstå.explanation: "At afstå" means "to give up" and "to refrain", to choose not to do or keep something. Before an action, it takes fra (from): at afstå fra at ryge (to refrain from smoking).

sentence.da: Han vil **afstå** fra at drikke kaffe efter klokken fire.
sentence.en: He will refrain from drinking coffee after four o'clock.

at afsætte.explanation: "At afsætte" means "to set aside" and "to sell". With time, money or space, it means setting it aside for a purpose. With goods, it means selling them: at afsætte varer (to sell goods).

sentence.da: Vi skal **afsætte** to timer til mødet i morgen.
sentence.en: We must set aside two hours for the meeting tomorrow.

at aftage.explanation: "At aftage" means "to decrease" or "to fade", for something that slowly gets weaker or smaller on its own, such as wind, noise or interest.

sentence.da: Smerten vil **aftage**, når medicinen begynder at virke.
sentence.en: The pain will ease when the medicine starts to work.

at aftale.explanation: "At aftale" means "to agree on" or "to arrange": two people settle a time or a plan together. The result is called en aftale (an agreement, an appointment).

sentence.da: Vi skal **aftale** en tid for mødet.
sentence.en: We have to arrange a time for the meeting.

at afvente.explanation: "At afvente" means "to await", to hold back until something happens. It takes the thing straight after it: afvente svar (await an answer), while at vente needs på: vente på svar (wait for an answer).

sentence.da: Vi må **afvente** lægens svar, før vi kan gøre mere.
sentence.en: We must await the doctor's answer before we can do more.

at afvise.explanation: "At afvise" means "to reject" or "to turn down", to say no to an offer, a person or an idea. To refuse to do something yourself, say at nægte: Han nægtede at betale (He refused to pay).

sentence.da: Banken vil **afvise** ansøgningen, hvis papirerne ikke er i orden.
sentence.en: The bank will reject the application if the papers are not in order.

at afværge.explanation: "At afværge" means "to avert", to stop something bad before it happens, such as an accident or a fight. To make something that has already happened less bad, use at afbøde (to mitigate).

sentence.da: Hun greb ind for at **afværge** et slagsmål.
sentence.en: She stepped in to avert a fight.

at agere.explanation: "At agere" means "to act", both on stage and in how a person behaves: Hun agerer roligt under pres (She acts calmly under pressure). Reacting to something is at reagere (to react).

sentence.da: Skuespilleren kan **agere** vred uden at sige et ord.
sentence.en: The actor can act angry without saying a word.

at analysere.explanation: "At analysere" means "to analyze": to study something closely by looking at its parts one by one. It is used for texts, numbers, samples and situations.

sentence.da: Laboratoriet skal **analysere** blodprøven og finde årsagen.
sentence.en: The lab must analyze the blood sample and find the cause.

at anbefale.explanation: "At anbefale" means "to recommend", for things you like and trust. It also works for advice about what to do: Lægen anbefaler hvile (The doctor recommends rest).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **anbefale** denne gode bog til dig.
sentence.en: I would like to recommend this good book to you.

at anbringe.explanation: "At anbringe" means "to place", to put something in a chosen spot: at anbringe en kasse (to place a box). It is also the official word for placing a child with another family or in care.

sentence.da: Kommunen kan **anbringe** barnet hos en plejefamilie.
sentence.en: The municipality can place the child with a foster family.

at ane.explanation: "At ane" means "to suspect" and "to have an idea", to feel something without knowing it for sure. It is mostly used in the negative: Jeg aner det ikke (I have no idea).

forms.en: I have had an idea / suspected

sentence.da: Hun må ikke **ane**, at vi planlægger en fest.
sentence.en: She must not suspect that we are planning a party.

at anerkende.explanation: "At anerkende" means "to recognize" or "to acknowledge": to openly accept that something is true or has value. For knowing a face again, use at genkende: Jeg genkender dig! (I recognize you!)

sentence.da: Landet vil ikke **anerkende** den nye regering.
sentence.en: The country will not recognize the new government.

at angive.explanation: "At angive" means "to state" or "to indicate": to give a clear fact, such as a price, a reason or a time. Han angiver tre grunde (He states three reasons).

sentence.da: Du skal **angive** din adresse på formularen.
sentence.en: You must state your address on the form.

at angre.explanation: "At angre" means "to regret". It is about something you did or chose and wish you had not.

sentence.da: Du vil ikke **angre**, at du kom.
sentence.en: You will not regret that you came.

at angribe.explanation: "At angribe" means "to attack", with weapons or with words. It is also used for an illness that harms a body part: Sygdommen angriber lungerne (The disease attacks the lungs).

sentence.da: Hæren vil **angribe** byen ved daggry.
sentence.en: The army will attack the city at dawn.

at angå.explanation: "At angå" means "to concern": to be about someone or to matter to them. It is mostly used as det angår (it concerns). A common phrase is hvad angår (as for): Hvad angår prisen, er den fin (As for the price, it is fine).

sentence.da: Den nye regel vil **angå** alle i huset.
sentence.en: The new rule will concern everyone in the house.

at anholde.explanation: "At anholde" means "to arrest": the police take a person into custody because of a suspected crime. You often meet it in news about the police, usually in the form Manden blev anholdt (The man was arrested).

sentence.da: Politiet kan **anholde** en mand, når han stjæler.
sentence.en: The police can arrest a man when he steals.

at anklage.explanation: "At anklage" means "to accuse" or "to charge": to say that someone has done something wrong. In court it is the prosecutor, en anklager, who charges a person with a crime. Outside court it is a strong claim: Hun anklager ham for at lyve (She accuses him of lying).

sentence.da: Han vil **anklage** hende for tyveri.
sentence.en: He will accuse her of theft.

at ankomme.explanation: "At ankomme" means "to arrive", and it sounds a bit formal, like an announcement for trains and planes. In everyday talk, Danes say at komme frem (to get there): Vi kommer frem klokken otte (We get there at eight).

sentence.da: Flyet skal **ankomme** klokken otte i aften.
sentence.en: The plane is due to arrive at eight tonight.

at anlægge.explanation: "At anlægge" means "to construct" and "to file (a lawsuit)". For building, it is used for larger works, such as roads, parks and railways. In law, it goes with sag (case): at anlægge sag mod en virksomhed (to bring a case against a company).

sentence.da: Kommunen vil **anlægge** en ny cykelsti langs vejen.
sentence.en: The municipality will construct a new bike path along the road.

at anmelde.explanation: "At anmelde" means "to report" a crime to the police, and also "to review" a book, film or concert: Hun anmelder film for en avis (She reviews films for a newspaper).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **anmelde** tyveriet til politiet i dag.
sentence.en: I will report the theft to the police today.

at anmode.explanation: "At anmode" means "to request", to formally ask an authority or an office for something, usually in writing. It is followed by om (for): at anmode om hjælp (to request help).

sentence.da: Han vil **anmode** om orlov i et halvt år.
sentence.en: He wants to request leave for half a year.

at annoncere.explanation: "At annoncere" means "to announce" or "to advertise": to make something known to many people at once. Bandet annoncerer en ny turné (The band announces a new tour).

sentence.da: Butikken vil **annoncere** udsalget i avisen.
sentence.en: The shop will advertise the sale in the newspaper.

at anse.explanation: "At anse" means "to regard" or "to consider": to hold the view that someone or something is of a certain kind. The pattern is anse X for Y: Jeg anser ham for ærlig (I consider him honest).

sentence.da: Vi må **anse** den gamle bro for farlig.
sentence.en: We must regard the old bridge as dangerous.

at anskaffe.explanation: "At anskaffe" means "to acquire": to get hold of something you need, such as equipment or a pet. Unlike at købe (to buy), it does not say how you get it: Vi anskaffer en hund (We are getting a dog).

sentence.da: Skolen vil **anskaffe** nye computere til eleverne.
sentence.en: The school will acquire new computers for the students.

at anslå.explanation: "At anslå" means "to estimate", to give a rough figure for a size, a cost or a number. Man anslår, at skaden koster en million (They estimate that the damage costs a million).

sentence.da: Eksperterne kan **anslå** prisen på huset.
sentence.en: The experts can estimate the price of the house.

at ansætte.explanation: "At ansætte" means "to hire". It means giving someone a job, not looking for one.

sentence.da: Vi vil gerne **ansætte** en ny kollega.
sentence.en: We would like to hire a new colleague.

at ansøge.explanation: "At ansøge" means "to apply": to formally ask for a job, a grant, a place or a permit. It is followed by om (for): Hun ansøger om et job (She applies for a job). To "apply" in the sense of "use" is at anvende (to use).

sentence.da: Du kan **ansøge** om en plads på skolen i marts.
sentence.en: You can apply for a place at the school in March.

at antage.explanation: "At antage" means "to assume": to take something as true without being sure. It is followed by at and what you assume: Jeg antager, at han kommer (I assume he is coming).

sentence.da: Vi må **antage**, at toget er forsinket.
sentence.en: We must assume that the train is delayed.

at antyde.explanation: "At antyde" means "to imply", to hint at something without stating it directly. It is often followed by at (that) and a short statement: Han antydede, at han var træt (He hinted that he was tired).

sentence.da: Han ville ikke sige det, men kun **antyde** det.
sentence.en: He did not want to say it, only to imply it.

at anvende.explanation: "At anvende" means "to use" or "to apply": to put a method, a rule or a tool to work. In everyday talk, at bruge (to use) is more common. Anvende fits methods, rules and materials: Man må ikke anvende mobilen under prøven (You may not use the phone during the test).

sentence.da: Læreren vil **anvende** en ny metode i timen.
sentence.en: The teacher will use a new method in class.

at appellere.explanation: "At appellere" means "to appeal", in the sense of calling on someone's feelings or sense of duty: Hun appellerer til vores medfølelse (She appeals to our compassion). Appealing a court ruling is a different word, at anke (to appeal a ruling).

sentence.da: Reklamen skal **appellere** til børn og forældre.
sentence.en: The ad must appeal to children and parents.

at applaudere.explanation: "At applaudere" means "to applaud": to clap your hands to show that you liked a performance. It is also used for approving of an idea or a decision: Jeg applauderer beslutningen (I applaud the decision).

sentence.da: Publikum vil **applaudere**, når koncerten er slut.
sentence.en: The audience will applaud when the concert is over.

at arbejde.explanation: "At arbejde" means "to work". Et arbejde also means "a job" or "work" itself: Jeg har meget arbejde (I have a lot of work).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **arbejde** på kontoret.
sentence.en: I have to work at the office.

at arbejde hjemmefra.explanation: "At arbejde hjemmefra" means "to work from home". Hjemmefra (from home) is one word, built from hjemme (at home) and fra (from). It is also used for leaving: Jeg går hjemmefra klokken otte (I leave home at eight).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **arbejde hjemmefra** på mandag.
sentence.en: I can work from home on Monday.

at arbejde med.explanation: "At arbejde med" means "to work with", and also to work in a field: Hun arbejder med dyr (She works with animals). For a place or a task, use på instead: Jeg arbejder på kontoret (I work at the office).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **arbejde med** børn.
sentence.en: I would like to work with children.

at arbejde på.explanation: "At arbejde på" means "to work at" a place, or "to work on" a task: Jeg arbejder på et hospital (I work at a hospital). Hun arbejder på et nyt projekt (She is working on a new project).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **arbejde på** min rapport i aften.
sentence.en: I want to work on my report tonight.

at argumentere.explanation: "At argumentere" means "to argue" in the sense of giving reasons for a view: Hun argumenterer for en kortere arbejdsuge (She argues for a shorter work week). To quarrel, use at skændes.

sentence.da: Når man skal **argumentere**, må man give gode grunde.
sentence.en: When you argue, you must give good reasons.

at arrangere.explanation: "At arrangere" means "to arrange" in the sense of planning and setting up something such as a party, a trip or a meeting. To put things in order is at ordne: Hun ordner bøgerne (She is putting the books in order).

sentence.da: Vi vil **arrangere** en fest for hele klassen.
sentence.en: We will arrange a party for the whole class.

at arrestere.explanation: "At arrestere" means "to arrest": the police take a person into custody. At anholde (to arrest) means almost the same and is the word you often see in news about the police.

sentence.da: Politiet har lov til at **arrestere** en mistænkt.
sentence.en: The police are allowed to arrest a suspect.

at arve.explanation: "At arve" means "to inherit": to receive money or things from someone who has died. It is also used for traits in a family: Hun har arvet sin mors blå øjne (She has inherited her mother's blue eyes).

sentence.da: Børnene skal **arve** huset, når deres far dør.
sentence.en: The children will inherit the house when their father dies.

atlanterhavet.explanation: "Atlanterhavet" means "the Atlantic Ocean", the large ocean west of Europe. Denmark has no coast on it, but the Faroe Islands lie in it.

forms.en: the coast of the Atlantic Ocean

sentence.da: Skibet sejler over **Atlanterhavet** fra Europa til Amerika.
sentence.en: The ship sails across the Atlantic Ocean from Europe to America.

atomkraft.explanation: "Atomkraft" means "nuclear power", electricity made by splitting atoms. Denmark does not produce it, so you mostly hear the word in debates about energy.

sentence.da: Sverige får en del af sin strøm fra **atomkraft**.
sentence.en: Sweden gets part of its electricity from nuclear power.

atten.explanation: "Atten" means "eighteen": Jeg er atten år (I am eighteen years old).

sentence.da: Min søn er **atten** år.
sentence.en: My son is eighteen years old.

atter.explanation: "Atter" means "again", the same as igen (again), but it sounds more formal and written: Hun er atter blevet syg (She has fallen ill again). In speech, Danes use igen.

sentence.da: Efter pausen begyndte musikken **atter** at spille.
sentence.en: After the break the music began to play again.

attraktiv.explanation: "Attraktiv" means "attractive", mostly about things that people want to have or choose: en attraktiv arbejdsplads (an attractive workplace). It can describe people too: en attraktiv mand (an attractive man).

sentence.da: Byen er **attraktiv** for unge, fordi der er mange uddannelser.
sentence.en: The city is attractive to young people because there are many programs of study.

august.explanation: "August" means "August". Danish writes month names with a small letter, so you write i august (in August), not i August.

sentence.da: Skolen starter igen i **august**.
sentence.en: School starts again in August.

australien.explanation: "Australien" means "Australia". Use i (in) for being there and til (to) for going there: Jeg bor i Australien (I live in Australia), Jeg rejser til Australien (I am traveling to Australia).

sentence.da: Kænguruer bor i **Australien**.
sentence.en: Kangaroos live in Australia.

autentisk.explanation: "Autentisk" means "authentic", true to the original: en autentisk italiensk pizza (an authentic Italian pizza). About a person it means true to themselves: Hun er meget autentisk (She is very true to herself).

sentence.da: Museets stol er **autentisk** og er over to hundrede år gammel.
sentence.en: The museum chair is authentic and is over two hundred years old.

automatisk.explanation: "Automatisk" means "automatic", something that happens by itself. The same word also tells how something happens: Døren åbner automatisk (The door opens automatically).

sentence.da: Lyset tændes **automatisk**, når du går ind.
sentence.en: The light comes on automatically when you walk in.

av.explanation: "Av" means "ouch" and is what you say when something hurts: Av, min fod! (Ouch, my foot!). For a small slip, say ups (oops) instead.

sentence.da: **Av**, den kop er varm!
sentence.en: Ouch, that cup is hot!

avanceret.explanation: "Avanceret" means "advanced", about things that are technically clever or at a high level. It can also hint that something is tricky to use: Programmet er for avanceret for mig (The program is too advanced for me).

sentence.da: Den nye telefon er meget **avanceret**, men let at bruge.
sentence.en: The new phone is very advanced, but easy to use.

en a-kasse.explanation: "En a-kasse" means "an unemployment insurance fund", an organization that Danes pay a monthly fee to, as protection for the time between jobs. The A stands for arbejdsløshed (unemployment).

sentence.da: Når jeg mister mit job, får jeg penge fra min **a-kasse**.
sentence.en: When I lose my job, I get money from my unemployment fund.

en abe.explanation: "En abe" means "a monkey", and also "an ape", because Danish uses one word for both. For a great ape, Danes say en menneskeabe (a great ape).

sentence.da: En **abe** klatrer op i det høje træ.
sentence.en: A monkey climbs up the tall tree.

en aborre.explanation: "En aborre" means "a perch", a common freshwater fish with a spiny fin on its back and orange-red fins below. It lives in Danish lakes and slow rivers.

sentence.da: Fisken med de mørke striber i søen er en **aborre**.
sentence.en: The fish with the dark stripes in the lake is a perch.

en abort.explanation: "En abort" means "an abortion", and also "a miscarriage" when it happens by itself. An extra word tells them apart: en provokeret abort (an induced abortion) and en spontan abort (a miscarriage).

sentence.da: En **abort** afslutter et svangerskab, før barnet bliver født.
sentence.en: An abortion ends a pregnancy before the baby is born.

en abrikos.explanation: "En abrikos" means "an apricot", a small orange fruit with soft skin and a large pit. It is often eaten dried.

sentence.da: En **abrikos** er lille og orange.
sentence.en: An apricot is small and orange.

en accent.explanation: "En accent" means "an accent", the way someone's speech sounds when they come from another region or language. It is also the small mark over a letter, like the é in café.

sentence.da: Hun taler dansk med en tydelig **accent**.
sentence.en: She speaks Danish with a clear accent.

en adgangskode.explanation: "En adgangskode" means "a password", a secret code that lets you in. It is built from adgang (access) and kode (code), and the same adgang is on the sign Ingen adgang (No entry).

sentence.da: Jeg har glemt min **adgangskode**.
sentence.en: I forgot my password.

en admiral.explanation: "En admiral" means "an admiral", a top officer in the navy. The matching top officer in the army is en general (a general).

sentence.da: En **admiral** leder mange skibe på havet.
sentence.en: An admiral leads many ships at sea.

en adoption.explanation: "En adoption" means "an adoption", when a child becomes the legal child of people who are not its birth parents. The verb at adoptere is also used for pets: adoptere en hund (to adopt a dog).

sentence.da: Ved **adoption** bliver barnet en del af en ny familie.
sentence.en: With adoption, the child becomes part of a new family.

en adresse.explanation: "En adresse" means "an address", the street and number where someone lives. You ask Hvad er din adresse? (What is your address?).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver min **adresse** på brevet: Vestergade 12.
sentence.en: I write my address on the letter: Vestergade 12.

en advarsel.explanation: "En advarsel" means "a warning", a message that danger or trouble may come.

sentence.da: Der er en **advarsel** om kraftig regn i dag.
sentence.en: There is a warning about heavy rain today.

en adventskrans.explanation: "En adventskrans" means "an Advent wreath", a ring of fir branches with four candles, set out in the weeks before December 24.

sentence.da: En **adventskrans** har fire lys, og vi tænder ét hver søndag.
sentence.en: An Advent wreath has four candles, and we light one each Sunday.

en advokat.explanation: "En advokat" means "a lawyer", someone who advises you about the law and argues your side in a dispute. The same word is used for men and women.

sentence.da: Jeg ringer til en **advokat**, fordi jeg har en retssag.
sentence.en: I am calling a lawyer because I have a court case.

en afbetaling.explanation: "En afbetaling" means "an installment plan", paying for something bit by bit instead of all at once. It is used with på: Danes say på afbetaling (on installments).

sentence.da: Sofaen kan købes på **afbetaling** over tolv måneder.
sentence.en: The sofa can be bought on installments over twelve months.

en afbrydelse.explanation: "En afbrydelse" means "an interruption", a stop in something that was going on, like a meeting, a call or the power. Unlike en pause (a break), an afbrydelse is usually not planned.

sentence.da: Vi kan arbejde i to timer uden **afbrydelse**.
sentence.en: We can work for two hours without interruption.

en afdeling.explanation: "En afdeling" means "a department", one section of a large organization, such as a hospital, a store or a bank.

sentence.da: Banken har en **afdeling** for lån.
sentence.en: The bank has a department for loans.

en afdelingsleder.explanation: "En afdelingsleder" means "a department manager", someone who runs one section of a shop, school, hospital or company. It is built from afdeling (department) and leder (leader).

sentence.da: En **afdelingsleder** har ansvaret for alle i sin afdeling.
sentence.en: A department manager is responsible for everyone in their department.

en affaldssortering.explanation: "En affaldssortering" means "a waste sorting", separating garbage into kinds so each kind can be reused.

sentence.da: Ved **affaldssortering** kommer glas, papir og plast i hver sin spand.
sentence.en: With waste sorting, glass, paper and plastic go in separate bins.

en affære.explanation: "En affære" means "an affair", a secret love relationship. It also means a matter or business, as in en dyr affære (an expensive business).

sentence.da: Han havde en hemmelig **affære** med en kollega.
sentence.en: He had a secret affair with a colleague.

en afgang.explanation: "En afgang" means "a departure", the time a train, bus or plane leaves.

sentence.da: Næste **afgang** er klokken ni.
sentence.en: The next departure is at nine.

en afgangseksamen.explanation: "En afgangseksamen" means "a final exam", the exam that closes a school or study program, where you show what you have learned.

sentence.da: Efter **afgangseksamen** får eleverne deres eksamensbevis.
sentence.en: After the final exam, the students get their diploma.

en afgift.explanation: "En afgift" means "a levy", a charge that the state requires you to pay on a thing or an activity, not on what you earn: en afgift på plastikposer (a levy on plastic bags).

sentence.da: Der er en høj **afgift** på cigaretter og alkohol i Danmark.
sentence.en: There is a high levy on cigarettes and alcohol in Denmark.

en afgrøde.explanation: "En afgrøde" means "a crop", a plant that farmers grow on farmland to sell as food, such as wheat or barley.

sentence.da: Raps er en gul **afgrøde**, og man laver olie af den.
sentence.en: Rapeseed is a yellow crop, and oil is made from it.

en afgørelse.explanation: "En afgørelse" means "a decision" or "a ruling", the final answer an authority gives after considering a case: Nævnets afgørelse er endelig (The board's ruling is final). Unlike en beslutning (a choice you make yourself), it settles a matter for others.

sentence.da: Kommunen sendte sin **afgørelse** med posten, og vi kan klage over den.
sentence.en: The municipality sent its decision by mail, and we can appeal it.

en afhandling.explanation: "En afhandling" means "a thesis", a serious piece of writing that studies one subject closely, usually at a university. A doctoral one is called en ph.d.-afhandling.

sentence.da: Når man skriver en lang **afhandling**, studerer man ét emne i dybden.
sentence.en: When you write a long thesis, you study one subject in depth.

en afhentning.explanation: "En afhentning" means "a pickup", collecting something that is ready for you, such as a parcel, an order or a child at daycare.

sentence.da: Du kan vælge **afhentning** i butikken i stedet for levering.
sentence.en: You can choose pickup in the store instead of delivery.

en afhængighed.explanation: "En afhængighed" means "an addiction" for drugs or alcohol, and "a dependence" when you need other people or things. Add af for what you depend on: afhængighed af hinanden (dependence on each other).

sentence.da: Hans **afhængighed** af spil kostede ham alle hans penge.
sentence.en: His addiction to gambling cost him all his money.

en afhøring.explanation: "En afhøring" means "an interrogation", the official questioning of a person by the police or in court. In Danish it is not necessarily harsh: it is the normal word for asking someone formally about what they know.

sentence.da: Ved en **afhøring** spørger politiet om, hvad der skete.
sentence.en: At an interrogation, the police ask what happened.

en afklaring.explanation: "En afklaring" means "a clarification", getting an open question settled. It is not the same as en forklaring (an explanation), which tells how or why something is.

sentence.da: Vi venter på en **afklaring**, før vi kan beslutte noget.
sentence.en: We are waiting for a clarification before we can decide anything.

en afkørsel.explanation: "En afkørsel" means "an exit" where you leave a big road. For the exit of a building, use en udgang (an exit) instead.

sentence.da: Tag næste **afkørsel** og drej til højre.
sentence.en: Take the next exit and turn right.

en aflevering.explanation: "En aflevering" means "a submission", a piece of schoolwork you give to the teacher by a set day. It is also used when you give something back: aflevering af nøgler (returning the keys).

sentence.da: Jeg skal skrive min **aflevering** færdig i aften.
sentence.en: I have to finish writing my submission tonight.

en afleveringsfrist.explanation: "En afleveringsfrist" means "a submission deadline", the last time you can hand in work, such as a school paper. It is built from at aflevere (to hand in) and frist (time limit).

sentence.da: Vi har en **afleveringsfrist** på fredag klokken tolv.
sentence.en: We have a submission deadline on Friday at twelve o'clock.

en aflysning.explanation: "En aflysning" means "a cancellation" of something planned, like a flight or a match.

sentence.da: Der kom en **aflysning** af flyet på grund af stormen.
sentence.en: There was a cancellation of the flight because of the storm.

en afløser.explanation: "En afløser" means "a substitute", a person who takes over someone's work for a while, for example when that person is sick or on vacation. Do not mix it up with en afløsning, which is the act of taking over.

sentence.da: Læreren er syg, og en **afløser** underviser klassen i dag.
sentence.en: The teacher is sick, and a substitute is teaching the class today.

en afløsning.explanation: "En afløsning" means "a relief" or "a replacement", the act of one person taking over from another at the same job. It is also used for help that gives a family caregiver a break: Hun får afløsning to timer om ugen (She gets relief two hours a week). The person who takes over is en afløser.

sentence.da: Når morgenholdet kommer, får natholdet **afløsning**.
sentence.en: When the morning team arrives, the night team gets relief.

en afrejse.explanation: "En afrejse" means "a departure", the moment you set off on a trip, often abroad. For a train or bus leaving a station, use afgang (departure) instead.

sentence.da: Vores **afrejse** er tidligt på fredag.
sentence.en: Our departure is early on Friday.

en afrikaner.explanation: "En afrikaner" means "an African", a person from Africa. Danish writes it with a small letter, unlike English.

sentence.da: Min nabo er **afrikaner** og kommer fra Kenya.
sentence.en: My neighbor is African and comes from Kenya.

en afsked.explanation: "En afsked" means "a farewell" or "a goodbye", the moment you part, often for a long time. It is the parting itself, not the word you say when leaving.

sentence.da: Vi tog **afsked** på stationen.
sentence.en: We said goodbye at the station.

en afslutning.explanation: "En afslutning" means "an ending" or "a conclusion", the last part of something, such as a speech or a school year.

sentence.da: Jeg kan godt lide filmens **afslutning**.
sentence.en: I like the ending of the film.

en afstand.explanation: "En afstand" means "a distance", the space between two places or people, measured in meters or kilometers. Hold afstand! means "Keep your distance!"

sentence.da: Der er en **afstand** på to kilometer til byen.
sentence.en: There is a distance of two kilometers to the town.

en afstemning.explanation: "En afstemning" means "a vote", when a group decides a question by voting, often yes or no. For choosing people for an office or a job, Danes say et valg (an election).

sentence.da: Ved en **afstemning** tæller man stemmerne, og flertallet vinder.
sentence.en: In a vote, you count the votes, and the majority wins.

en aftale.explanation: "En aftale" means "an appointment" or "an agreement". An appointment: en aftale med tandlægen (an appointment with the dentist). A deal: Det er en aftale! (It's a deal!).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **aftale** med lægen.
sentence.en: I have an appointment with the doctor.

en aften.explanation: "En aften" means "an evening", the time of day between afternoon and night. Useful phrases are i aften (tonight), om aftenen (in the evening, as a habit), and god aften (good evening).

sentence.da: Vi spiser mad hver **aften**.
sentence.en: We eat food every evening.

en aftenrutine.explanation: "En aftenrutine" means "an evening routine", the things you do each night before bed, such as brushing your teeth or reading.

sentence.da: Min **aftenrutine** er te, en bog og tidlig seng.
sentence.en: My evening routine is tea, a book and an early bed.

en aftenskole.explanation: "En aftenskole" means "an evening class", a course for adults who learn something in their free time, such as cooking or painting.

sentence.da: Min mor går på **aftenskole** for at lære spansk.
sentence.en: My mother goes to evening classes to learn Spanish.

en aftentur.explanation: "En aftentur" means "an evening walk", a calm walk after dinner. It is built from aften (evening) and tur (walk, trip), and tur also works alone: Skal vi tage en tur? (Shall we go for a walk?)

sentence.da: Efter maden tager vi en **aftentur** langs vandet.
sentence.en: After dinner we take an evening walk along the water.

en aftrækker.explanation: "En aftrækker" means "a trigger", the small lever on a gun that you pull to shoot. For something that sets off a reaction, use en udløser (a trigger).

sentence.da: Pistolen har en **aftrækker**, som man trykker på for at skyde.
sentence.en: The pistol has a trigger that you press to shoot.

en afveksling.explanation: "En afveksling" means "a variety" or "a change", something different that breaks up a routine. It is common in til afveksling (for a change): Til afveksling lavede han mad (For a change, he cooked). Do not mix it up with en udveksling (an exchange).

sentence.da: Efter mange dage inde var en tur i skoven en dejlig **afveksling**.
sentence.en: After many days indoors, a walk in the forest was a lovely change.

en afvigelse.explanation: "En afvigelse" means "a deviation", a difference from what is normal, expected or planned: en afvigelse fra planen (a deviation from the plan).

sentence.da: Termometeret viser en **afvigelse** på to grader fra normalen.
sentence.en: The thermometer shows a deviation of two degrees from normal.

en agent.explanation: "En agent" means "an agent", someone who acts for another person and handles their deals. It also means a spy: en hemmelig agent (a secret agent).

sentence.da: En **agent** forhandler kontrakter for en skuespiller eller atlet.
sentence.en: An agent negotiates contracts for an actor or athlete.

en agurk.explanation: "En agurk" means "a cucumber", a long, green vegetable that is crisp and watery. Pickled ones are syltede agurker (pickled cucumbers).

sentence.da: Jeg skærer en **agurk** til salaten.
sentence.en: I am cutting a cucumber for the salad.

en airbag.explanation: "En airbag" means "an airbag", the cushion that fills with air in a crash to protect the people in the car.

sentence.da: Min nye bil har en **airbag** i rattet.
sentence.en: My new car has an airbag in the steering wheel.

en airfryer.explanation: "En airfryer" means "an air fryer", a small oven that cooks with hot air and little oil, so food turns crispy.

sentence.da: Man kan lave pommes frites i en **airfryer**.
sentence.en: You can make fries in an air fryer.

en aktie.explanation: "En aktie" means "a share" in a company. Its price changes every day, and it can pay money back to its owner each year, called udbytte (a dividend).

sentence.da: Når man køber en **aktie**, ejer man en lille del af firmaet.
sentence.en: When you buy a share, you own a small part of the company.

en aktiekurs.explanation: "En aktiekurs" means "a share price", what one piece of a company costs to buy right now. It changes all the time while the market is open.

sentence.da: Hvis mange vil købe en aktie, stiger dens **aktiekurs**.
sentence.en: If many people want to buy a share, its share price rises.

en aktivitet.explanation: "En aktivitet" means "an activity", something you do for fun or to keep fit, like hiking or board games. It is also used for things a school or club plans for people to do: aktiviteter for børn (activities for children).

sentence.da: Svømning er en sjov **aktivitet** for hele familien.
sentence.en: Swimming is a fun activity for the whole family.

en akvariefisk.explanation: "En akvariefisk" means "an aquarium fish", a fish kept at home in a tank. It is built from akvarium (aquarium) and fisk (fish), and fisk is also in en fiskestang (a fishing rod).

sentence.da: En **akvariefisk** lever i et akvarium med planter.
sentence.en: An aquarium fish lives in an aquarium with plants.

en alarm.explanation: "En alarm" means "an alarm", both a warning sound and the wake-up alarm on a phone: Alarmen gik i nat (The alarm went off last night). To turn it off, say Jeg slukker alarmen (I turn off the alarm).

sentence.da: Min **alarm** ringer klokken seks hver morgen.
sentence.en: My alarm rings at six every morning.

en alarmklokke.explanation: "En alarmklokke" means "an alarm bell", a bell that sounds to warn people. It is built from alarm (alarm) and klokke (bell). Klokke also means "clock", which is why you ask the time with Hvad er klokken? (What time is it?)

sentence.da: Vi hørte en **alarmklokke** ringe midt om natten.
sentence.en: We heard an alarm bell ring in the middle of the night.

en albue.explanation: "En albue" means "an elbow". Danish often says the elbow where English says my elbow: Jeg har slået albuen is literally I have hit the elbow, meaning "I have hit my elbow". Min albue (my elbow) is also fine.

sentence.da: Armen bøjer ved din **albue**.
sentence.en: The arm bends at your elbow.

en alder.explanation: "En alder" means "an age", how old someone is. To ask, Danes say Hvor gammel er du? (How old are you?) with gammel (old), not alder. You will also see it in i min alder (at my age).

sentence.da: På blanketten skal du skrive din **alder**.
sentence.en: On the form, you have to write your age.

en algoritme.explanation: "En algoritme" means "an algorithm", a set of rules that a computer follows to solve a problem or make a choice. Apps use algorithms to decide what to show you.

sentence.da: En **algoritme** er en række trin, som computeren følger.
sentence.en: An algorithm is a series of steps that the computer follows.

en alkoholiker.explanation: "En alkoholiker" means "an alcoholic", a person who is dependent on alcohol and finds it very hard to stop drinking.

sentence.da: Som **alkoholiker** kan han ikke drikke bare ét glas.
sentence.en: As an alcoholic he cannot drink even one glass.

en allergi.explanation: "En allergi" means "an allergy", when your body reacts badly to something like nuts, pollen or cats. It joins with other words, with allergi at the end: en pollenallergi (a pollen allergy).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **allergi** mod nødder.
sentence.en: I have an allergy to nuts.

en alliance.explanation: "En alliance" means "an alliance", an agreement between countries or groups to support each other, often in politics or war.

sentence.da: Landene dannede en **alliance** for at beskytte hinanden.
sentence.en: The countries formed an alliance to protect each other.

en allieret.explanation: "En allieret" means "an ally", a country or person that stands on your side and helps you in a conflict. In history, De Allierede (the Allies) were the countries that fought Germany in World War II.

sentence.da: Hvis et land er din **allieret**, hjælper det dig i krig.
sentence.en: If a country is your ally, it helps you in war.

en altan.explanation: "En altan" means "a balcony", the small outdoor space attached to an apartment.

sentence.da: Vi sidder på vores **altan** og nyder solen.
sentence.en: We sit on our balcony and enjoy the sun.

en amatør.explanation: "En amatør" means "an amateur", someone who does something for love of it and not as a paid job. It can also be an insult for a person who does a poor job: Sikke en amatør! (What an amateur!)

sentence.da: Han er **amatør** og spiller fodbold uden at få penge.
sentence.en: He is an amateur and plays soccer without getting paid.

en ambassade.explanation: "En ambassade" means "an embassy", one country's office in another country, where its citizens can get help.

sentence.da: Vi fik hjælp fra den danske **ambassade** i Rom.
sentence.en: We got help from the Danish embassy in Rome.

en ambassadør.explanation: "En ambassadør" means "an ambassador", the top representative of one country in another, who works at en ambassade (an embassy). It is also used for a well-known person who speaks for a brand or a cause.

sentence.da: Hver **ambassadør** repræsenterer sit land i udlandet.
sentence.en: Each ambassador represents their country abroad.

en ambition.explanation: "En ambition" means "an ambition", a strong wish to achieve something big in your work or life. The usual phrase is at have ambitioner (to have ambitions).

sentence.da: Hun har en stor **ambition** om at blive læge.
sentence.en: She has a big ambition to become a doctor.

en ambulance.explanation: "En ambulance" means "an ambulance", a vehicle that takes sick or hurt people to the hospital. In an emergency in Denmark, you call 112.

sentence.da: Han er meget syg. Ring efter en **ambulance**!
sentence.en: He is very sick. Call for an ambulance!

en amerikaner.explanation: "En amerikaner" means "an American", a person from the USA, used for both men and women. It does not start with a capital letter: Hun er amerikaner (She is an American).

sentence.da: Hun er **amerikaner** og bor i Danmark.
sentence.en: She is American and lives in Denmark.

en analyse.explanation: "En analyse" means "an analysis", a careful look that breaks something into parts to understand it. It is used for data, texts and blood tests alike.

sentence.da: Efter en grundig **analyse** kender vi årsagen til problemet.
sentence.en: After a thorough analysis we know the cause of the problem.

en ananas.explanation: "En ananas" means "a pineapple", a tropical fruit with a rough, spiky skin and juicy flesh.

sentence.da: En **ananas** er sød og gul indeni.
sentence.en: A pineapple is sweet and yellow inside.

en anbefaling.explanation: "En anbefaling" means "a recommendation", advice about what is good or what you should do, from a friend or from a doctor.

sentence.da: Tak for din **anbefaling** af restauranten.
sentence.en: Thanks for your recommendation of the restaurant.

en and.explanation: "En and" means "a duck". Watch out: anden also means "the other" or "second", as in den anden (the other one), so the rest of the sentence shows which is meant.

sentence.da: En **and** svømmer på søen.
sentence.en: A duck is swimming on the lake.

en andel.explanation: "En andel" means "a share" or "a portion", a part of a whole: andelen af ældre vokser (the share of older people is growing). In housing, an andelsbolig (co-op apartment) is one where you own a share of the building.

sentence.da: Hver af os betaler en lige stor **andel** af regningen.
sentence.en: Each of us pays an equal share of the bill.

en andelsbolig.explanation: "En andelsbolig" means "a cooperative apartment", a home in a building that the residents own together. You pay a monthly fee for it instead of owning the walls yourself. It is common in Danish cities.

sentence.da: I en **andelsbolig** ejer du en andel af foreningen, ikke selve lejligheden.
sentence.en: In a cooperative apartment you own a share of the association, not the apartment itself.

en anekdote.explanation: "En anekdote" means "an anecdote", a short episode from real life that you tell to others, often about a person and often with a laugh.

sentence.da: Han fortalte en sjov **anekdote** om sin første dag på arbejde.
sentence.en: He told a funny anecdote about his first day at work.

en anelse.explanation: "En anelse" means "a hint" or "a slight idea". It names a tiny amount: en anelse bedre (a touch better). It also names a vague idea of something, and is common in questions: Har du en anelse om hvorfor? (Do you have any idea why?)

sentence.da: Jeg har ikke den mindste **anelse** om, hvor nøglerne er.
sentence.en: I do not have the slightest idea where the keys are.

en anfører.explanation: "En anfører" means "a captain (team)", the player who is in charge of a sports team on the field. It comes from at anføre (to lead), so it can also mean the leader of any group.

sentence.da: Hun er holdets **anfører** og leder spillerne på banen.
sentence.en: She is the team's captain and leads the players on the field.

en angriber.explanation: "En angriber" means "a forward / attacker", a player whose job is to score goals. Outside of sport, it is a person who carries out an assault on someone.

sentence.da: En **angriber** skal score mål, mens forsvaret skal stoppe modstanderen.
sentence.en: A forward must score goals, while the defense must stop the opponent.
